hero.label: Editorial Event Photographer
hero.title: Event Coverage
hero.subtext: Editorial photography for launches, meetups, and community nights. Same-day selects, full gallery within 72 hours, text-based English coordination throughout.
hero.sideBody: A Tokyo developer meetup photographed as an editorial sequence: arrival light, branded details, focused conversations, and the afterglow of a room full of builders.

gallery.label: Selected Frames
gallery.title: A contact sheet with heat still in it.
gallery.subtitle: Scenes from Cafe Cursor Tokyo, a developer meetup in Tokyo.
gallery.intro: The page is not a uniform grid on purpose. It moves from hero frames into a tighter contact sheet so the event reads like a sequence, not a folder dump.
gallery.sheetNote: 11-frame edit. Atmosphere, people, and product energy.

services.label: Coverage Design
services.title: Coverage shaped for speed, atmosphere, and reuse.
services.intro: Each deliverable is designed to help your team publish quickly without flattening the mood of the event.

eventPhotography.title: Event Photography
eventPhotography.description: Candid interaction, keynote moments, sponsor visibility, and the quieter scenes that make a community feel real.

highlightVideos.title: Highlight Videos
highlightVideos.description: Short-form recaps built for social and internal sharing, cut to keep the event's rhythm rather than just summarizing the agenda.

sameDayDelivery.title: Same-Day Delivery
sameDayDelivery.description: A fast-turn workflow for organizers who need polished selects while guests are still posting and the room is still warm.

testimonial.label: Case Study
testimonial.title: A developer meetup edited like a lived-in story.
testimonial.intro: This case called for more than clean event coverage: the images had to preserve warmth, show product context, and still be useful for recap, social, and future promotion.
testimonial.focusBody: Arrival light, table conversations, branded details, and the smaller cues that make a developer room feel real all had to remain visible in the edit.
testimonial.deliverablesBody: Same-day selects, an edited gallery for recap and reuse, and detail frames that could travel across social, decks, and future event pages.
testimonial.approachBody: The sequence moves between hero frames and quieter details so the event reads as a story rather than a flat archive.

about.label: Why Me
about.title: I understand tech events
about.titleSub: because I already belong in the room.
about.body: I am both a full-stack engineer and an event photographer, so I can read what people respond to and which moments will matter later in tech contexts.

points.communityBody: I know which interactions matter because I already understand the culture around launches, demos, and meetups.
points.bilingualBody: Inquiries, pre-event briefs, and delivery notes work smoothly in written English — the way distributed teams already coordinate.
points.deliveryBody: The workflow is optimized to move quickly without making the output feel generic.

form.heading: Let's shape the next event with intention.
form.subheading: Share the event basics below. I will reply within 24 hours with availability and the best coverage shape for your format.
form.asideBody: The inquiry starts with logistics, but the work is editorial. I plan for flow, key people, and what the images need to do after the event.

notes.englishSupportBody: Email, DM, and pre-event documents work in English. Text-based coordination keeps everything clear from first inquiry through delivery.
notes.deliverablesBody: Same-day selects, full gallery within 72 hours, optional highlight video.
notes.eventScopeBody: Tech meetups, product launches, community gatherings, and small-to-mid scale branded events.

demo.title: WebGL Study #01 — Distortion Hover
demo.description: GLSL displacement mapping applied to portrait photographs, creating organic hover transitions between image pairs. A reinterpretation of Codrops' distortion technique with original photography.
demo.credit: Inspired by Codrops WebGL Distortion Hover Effects

film-lab.title: WebGL Study #05 — Film Lab
film-lab.description: A real-time color grading tool in the browser. Drop images or videos, then adjust exposure, contrast, and LUT in real-time. The effect chain follows DaVinci Resolve's color page pipeline, implemented entirely in GPU fragment shaders.
